title: Attention under Bounded Key-Query Similarity: Space Complexity and Transformer Anisotropy
summary: This is a theoretical space-complexity analysis of KV-cache compression under bounded key-query cosine similarity, not a deployable replacement for an existing method; its practical content is a proof that simple uniform sampling of cached tokens is nearly space-optimal for typical parameter regimes. It costs nothing to adopt since it introduces no new algorithm, but it also delivers no measured memory or latency improvement on real workloads. The risk is over-reading the result: optimality is worst-case under a similarity model, so uniform sampling may still underperform learned or attention-aware eviction on specific models and tasks.
rationale: The paper provides theoretical justification for an already-available heuristic rather than a validated new method, so the reader should note it as supporting evidence for uniform-sampling KV-cache compression but not treat it as an adoptable artifact.
